BBC, 25 Nov 2026 14:23 GMT

New drones could tackle crime 'within 30 seconds'

New drones with speakers, similar to the one pictured above, could be introduced to tackle crime

Black drone with speaker attached to it. It is flying above a blurred crowd.

New drones featuring loud speakers and spotlights could be introduced in a town centre to clamp down on crime.

It is hoped the first trial will begin in March 2027, when a drone will be placed on top of Swindon's fire station that can be deployed to incidents as they unfold.

Philip Wilkinson OBE, Police and Crime Commissioner (PCC) for Wiltshire, said the drone could \"cover anywhere\" in the town centre.

\"If you can imagine an incident where perhaps somebody is being threatened, probably within 30 seconds we can have a drone over them with a spotlight on the potential offender, and talk to them telling them that their actions are being recorded,\" he added.

Councillor Matt Hinton, from Swindon Borough Council, said he \"welcomed\" the proposal and added that the speakers on some cameras in car parks were already helping \"deter\" anti-social behaviour.

Wilkinson said information could be live streamed via the drone \"back to the control room\" where they could then deploy the \"appropriate assets\".

It is hoped the drone could also be flown from other sites such as Gablecross Police Station, according to the Local Democracy Reporting Service.

\"If we can make this work in Swindon, we will then take it around the county, not only in the town centres, but also into the rural crime hotspots,\" Wilkinson said.

Wilkinson said if the trial was successful in Swindon, they would expand it across Wiltshire

Over the last few years, Swindon has become a growing hub for drone manufacturing.

In June, The Ministry of Defence (MoD) opened a drone site at Panattoni Park and earlier this month, a new site for manufacturing drones on Paddington Drive opened.

The latest plan for drones to deter anti-social behaviour was announced following a visit from the superintendent running the National Police Chiefs' Council drone programme.

Hinton said: \"When someone hears a voice asking them to stop, they know somebody has seen what's happening and can do something about it.\"

\"The same principle could work in the wider town centre. If a drone can reach someone who's being threatened within 30 seconds, police could speak directly to the person threatening them while guiding officers to the scene.\"

\"For the person on the receiving end, hearing a police voice and knowing help is on the way could make a real difference,\" he added.

Wilkinson said that some issues still need to be resolved with the Civil Aviation Authority, but that they hope to be able to start the first trial in March.

Additional reporting by Holly Rattley

British people, particularly teens and young adults, are having less or no sex compared to past generations, but lots are watching porn and sexting, a major study suggests.

It is the first time The National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles' (Natsal) research into general public sex lives has asked about online behaviours.

The latest results were published in The Lancet and were based on a survey of 6,700 people aged 16–59 who were selected at random across Britain.

Energy bills will rise by 26% for millions of households in January, the highest rate in nearly four years, after a surge in gas prices sparked by the Iran war.

Isaac, a student at Durham University, said he had no choice but to keep the heating in his student house on 'constantly' due to poor insulation, and he was not looking forward to the price increase.

In the Autumn budget, the government announced a one-off payment of £100 for households in council bands A to D, 'half a weekly shop' according to Isaac.
